/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 27 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2666 (1)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4282 (0)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1957 (-3)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1540 (5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 802 (5)
CAPESIZE
It has been a subdued start to the week, with activity notably muted ahead of the shorter trading week due to the Labour Day holiday on Friday. The BCI 182 5TC remained effectively flat, edging up by just $1 to close at $38,837, reflecting the lack of fresh momentum across both basins. In the Pacific, trading conditions were particularly quiet despite underlying fundamentals appearing supportive. Cargo volumes remain healthy, with a noticeable uptick in coal stems and tenders, although this has yet to translate into firmer rates. The C5 index inched up by $0.030 to $13.030, with fixtures reported around the $13.00 level. Two major miners were active, but overall participation remained limited. The Atlantic basin saw a sluggish start, continuing the stand-off observed at the end of last week. Activity was thin, with little to drive rates in either direction, although the C3 index eased slightly by $0.036 to $33.032. Tight ballaster supply for May loaders persists, which may offer some underlying support if demand improves.
PANAMAX
A subdued start to the week with the same underlying tones from last week being carried across. In the Atlantic, market participants are echoing about a build up of tonnage in the North Continent with a relatively limited number of transatlantic stems. This, in turn, is placing additional pressure on the fronthaul market from the US Gulf and North Coast South America, as competition for available cargoes intensifies. This negative sentiment is reflected in today’s index, as the P1A and P2A declined by $109 and $337 respectively. A more positive day in Asia, with several reported fixtures for both long and short duration cargoes, while the gains seen in recent weeks continue to hold. Sentiment remains firm, supported by healthy cargo flow from East Coast Australia and the North Pacific. Reported period fixtures have been quiet today and the P5TC fell by $21 to $17,617.

Asia
Da Tang 712 (75,509 2012) Sual 28 April fixed for a trip via Indonesia to South China, but further details lacked. The scrubber fitted Aquavita Glory (81,668 2020) CJK 27/28 April fixed an Australian round voyage at $20,000 to Richland. Messrs Tongli fixed the Canon Trader (82,200 2024) Rizhao 1 May for an Australian round voyage although there was some debate over the daily hire rate, ranging from around $22,000 to $22,500. Tongli were also said to have fixed the Marielena (81,354 2008) Yuhuan 29/30 April at $19,000 for an Australian round trip. The scrubber fitted Taho Circular (84,484 2022) Kakogawa 1 May was said to have fixed on subjects for a Pacific round voyage in the $22,000s. Post Marvel (95,711 2013) CJK 1/4 May was also said to have been placed on subjects, but no other information came to light. Athanasia C (81,488 2012) Hong Kong 26/28 April was said to have fixed but further information was yet to appear.
SUPRAMAX
A typical Monday with little in the way of fresh activity as both sides play the usual waiting and collecting game. The Atlantic remained generally unchanged from the end of last week, although again some felt that there was a slight easing from the South Atlantic. It surfaced that the Pride of Yasna (56,019 2006) open Otranto was heard fixed to EC India with fertiliser at $18,000, but no more details emerged. Brokers described a positional start from Asia, with various upcoming holidays during the week some thinking demand may ease from the north. The 11TC average did however register a $65 gain to finish the day at $19,468.
HANDYSIZE
The week continued a similar trajectory from the end of last week. With little sign of much fresh enquiry from the Continent-Mediterranean. The US Gulf and South Atlantic bucking that trend as stronger rates were being discussed, brokers said. The Asian arena was a slightly more cautious start with some thinking that fresh enquiry from the faith had eased since the end of last week. Period activity remained in hand, The Tao Mariner (25,064 2010) open China 3/6 May was heard fixed for 3/5 months trading at $13,500 but no more details surfaced. Also a Tess 42,000 newbuilding ex yard August 2026 was heard fixed for 3 years at 122 per cent of BHSI, again further details remained under wraps.

Atlantic
The Stade (35,480 2015) was heard fixed delivery Çanakkale for a trip redelivery Florida at $10,750 (plus $150,000 ILOHC) with cement to Oldendorff.

Asia
The Rosalia (39,907 2016) open CJK was heard fixed at $16,500 with further split rate to the Continent with Pan Ocean, but further details remained undisclosed. Also, a 40,000 open South China was rumoured fixed for multi legs in the high $17,000s, but no more details surfaced.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Iron Ore Stockpiles Continue to Fall

In the week to 24 April, Chinese iron ore stockpiles fell for the third consecutive week, down 1.0 Mt to 165.9 Mt, the lowest level since January, according to data from 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal. Despite the decline, inventories remained 23.8 Mt above the year-ago level. Hot metal output at Chinese steel mills held at 2.4 Mt/day, MySteel data show, adding to destocking at ports and signalling firm iron ore demand during the week. Seaborne iron ore prices at Chinese ports stayed firm at around 786 yuan/t on 24 April.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher despite a relatively unchanged physical market, with the index only gaining $1. The biggest move was in the May contract with 33750 paid, followed by the Jun with 32500 paid. The May v Jun spread widened and strengthened up to +1000. We saw some early resistance on the Q34 following on from Fridays Bauxite mining news, however with he front so well supported, Q3 was eventually paid to 30000 and Q4 29950, as the Q3 v Q4 prints +50. Cal27 liquidity was choppy with 25500 trading early on, then paid up to a high of 25750 during the afternoon rally.

PMX
A quiet start to the week for the pmx market with rates rising across the whole of the curve to last Friday's close. May was paid at a high of 19100 and saw a low of 18750 finishing the day at 19000. Jun bounced around 19400 - 19100. Q3 printed 18450 up to 18750 and the Q3/Q4 spread traded at 1400. There was no participation on the cal today.

SMX + HANDY
Limited trading to start the week, as buyers emerged to start and the front of the SMX curve opened firm. Said support was not sustained and the prompt months slowly drifted from the highs over the course of the day. May traded 18000 to 17500, Jun from 17900 to 17500 and May+Jun at 18000. In contrast the back end held value, Q3 trading 16600 – 16700, Q4 at 15450 and Q3+Q4 between 16050 – 16150. The Handy market traded around Friday’s levels as May+Jun traded 15800, Jun traded 16250 and Q2 was paid at 15150.

Chinese Iron Ore Stockpiles Continue to Fall
In the week to 24 April, Chinese iron ore stockpiles fell for
the third consecutive week, down 1.0 Mt to 165.9 Mt, the
lowest level since January, according to data from 42 portside
locations monitored by Umetal. Despite the decline,
inventories remained 23.8 Mt above the year-ago level. Hot
metal output at Chinese steel mills held at 2.4 Mt/day,
MySteel data show, adding to destocking at ports and
signalling ﬁrm iron ore demand during the week. Seaborne
iron ore prices at Chinese ports stayed ﬁrm at around 786
yuan/t on 24 April.

Cape Routes

c5 may traded in a few smaller clips from 13.05 - 13.10,

unchanged physical market, with the index only gaining $1.

resistance on the Q34 following on from Fridays Bauxite

prints +50. Cal27 liquidity was choppy with 25500 trading

Despite the decline, inventories remained 23.8 Mt above the year-ago level. Hot metal output at Chinese steel mills held at 2.4 Mt/day, MySteel data show, adding to destocking at ports and signalling firm iron ore demand during the week. Seaborne iron ore prices at Chinese ports stayed firm at around 786 yuan/t on 24 April. Trading Commentary Cape Routes The route markets started the week on a positive tone. The c5 may traded in a few smaller clips from 13.05 - 13.10, closing valued at 13.15. The c3 also moved higher with the may contract trading from 32 in the morning session up to 32.85 late on. Cape The Cape FFA curve rallied higher despite a relatively unchanged physical market, with the index only gaining $1. The biggest move was in the May contract with 33750 paid, followed by the Jun with 32500 paid. The May v Jun spread widened and strengthened up to +1000. We saw some early resistance on the Q34 following on from Fridays Bauxite mining news, however with he front so well supported, Q3 was eventually paid to 30000 and Q4 29950, as the Q3 v Q4 prints +50. Cal27 liquidity was choppy with 25500 trading early on, then paid up to a high of 25750 during the afternoon rally. PMX A quiet start to the week for the pmx market with rates rising across the whole of the curve to last Friday's close. May was paid at a high of 19100 and saw a low of 18750 finishing the day at 19000. Jun bounced around 19400 - 19100. Q3 printed 18450 up to 18750 and the Q3/Q4 spread traded at 1400. There was no participation on the cal today. SMX + HANDY Limited trading to start the week, as buyers emerged to start and the front of the SMX curve opened firm. Said support was not sustained and the prompt months slowly drifted from the highs over the course of the day. May traded 18000 to 17500, Jun from 17900 to 17500 and May+Jun at 18000. In contrast the back end held value, Q3 trading 16600 – 16700, Q4 at 15450 and Q3+Q4 between 16050 – 16150. ai_analysis.summary: 27日波罗的海干散货指数整体平稳，BDI微涨1点至2666，各船型走势分化：Capesize持平，Supramax和Handysize小幅上涨，Panamax小幅回落。市场受五一假期前交易清淡影响，太平洋地区煤炭货盘有所增加但费率支撑有限，大西洋地区表现疲软，North Continent运力积压持续施压。FFA市场Capesize和Panamax合约曲线前移月大幅上涨，显示市场对近期前景保持相对乐观。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize市场受假期因素影响活跃度下降，太平洋C5微涨，大西洋C3走弱，运力供应充足限制上行空间。Panamax大西洋端承压，North Continent积压运力挤压跨大西洋及美湾货盘竞争，亚洲端基本面仍显稳健。Supramax和Handysize在美湾及南大西洋区域表现相对强劲，支撑整体费率。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize 5TC即期费率$38,837，基本持平；FFA May26合约跳涨$2,300至33,750-34,000区间，曲线前端强势。Panamax P5TC跌$21至$17,617，May合约逆势上扬$275至18,900-19,000，显示短期预期仍乐观。Supramax 11TC涨$65至$19,468，Handysize HSATC涨$120至$13,675，区域分化明显。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注C3（大西洋-太平洋）和C5（太平洋铁矿航线）价差变化，C3贴水走阔反映大西洋需求疲软。Panamax亚洲端费率能否维持强势并支撑整体指数。FFA市场Capesize May合约流动性增强，关注近月价差收敛机会。假期后需求端实质改善情况，尤其是煤炭和铁矿货盘。

market_watch: Capesize C3大西洋航线小幅走弱，FFA May26跳涨$2,300显示期货市场仍看多近月
Panamax大西洋端承压，North Continent运力积压持续施压P1A和P2A
Supramax S2（北中国-澳洲往返）涨$100至$19,481，太平洋航线需求稳健
Handysize HS4（美湾-欧陆）大涨$279至$13,679，美湾区域强势延续
FFA曲线倒挂结构未变，Cal27仍贴水于即期，长远期预期谨慎

route_focus.view: C3航线（大西洋-太平洋）即期费率$33.032，跌$0.036，受大西洋端疲软需求拖累。运力供应充足压制费率，但tight ballaster供给或提供底部支撑。短期料维持区间震荡。
P1A航线（美湾-欧陆）即期下跌$109至$17,508水平。North Continent运力积压导致竞争加剧，fronthaul货盘承压。亚洲端基本面尚可，短期P1A仍面临下行压力，关注假期后需求恢复情况。
HS1航线（Skaw-Passero-南美东海岸）即期$7,886，跌$28。相对HS3（南美东海岸返欧）大涨$267至$23,050，回程航线明显强于去程。显示南美东海岸粮食出货活跃，支撑返程费率。
